items.en: Nagoya's flat, wide, ribbon-thin wheat noodle in the same clear broth
items.note: The Nagoya noodle: rolled thin and cut broad, so it cooks fast and carries far more broth per mouthful than round udon — softer, more slippery, less chew. Usually finished with katsuobushi flakes, aburaage and greens. Wheat, and the broth is wheat soy plus bonito dashi.

items.en: Plain hot buckwheat soba in the house broth
items.note: Neighbourhood soba, wheat-blended rather than pure buckwheat — this is a udon shop that also makes soba, not the reverse. Wheat noodle and wheat-soy broth.

items.en: Large portion of any of the three plain noodles above
items.note: A footnote adds that koro — the chilled version served with cold broth poured over, a Nagoya summer habit — costs ¥30 more on any bowl.

items.en: Udon topped with sweet-simmered fried tofu pouches (aburaage), kamaboko and leek
items.note: A Nagoya-area name for what elsewhere is kitsune udon. The aburaage is stewed in soy and sugar until it drips, and it slowly sweetens the whole broth. Wheat noodle, wheat-soy broth, bonito dashi.

items.en: Udon scattered with tenkasu — crisp scraps of fried tempura batter
items.note: The tenkasu soften and release their oil into the broth, which is exactly the effect you're paying for. Pure wheat on wheat.

items.en: Udon with beaten egg swirled into the simmering broth so it sets in soft ribbons
items.note: 'Toji' means to bind or close — the egg thickens the broth and turns it cloudy and comforting. The standard order when you're unwell. Wheat noodle, wheat-soy broth.

items.en: Udon under a thick, glossy starch-thickened broth that stays scalding hot
items.note: The starch traps the heat, so this arrives far hotter than it looks — approach it carefully. Usually finished with ginger. Thickened with potato starch, but the broth underneath is wheat soy and the noodle is wheat.

items.en: Udon with thin slices of beef simmered in soy and sugar
items.note: The beef fat films the broth and makes it noticeably richer than the plain bowl. Wheat noodle, wheat-soy braise.

items.en: Udon in a thick Japanese curry broth — dashi and curry roux, thickened to a gravy
items.note: One of the dishes this shop is known for locally, and a Nagoya lunchtime staple. Japanese curry roux is built on wheat flour and butter, on top of a bonito-dashi and wheat-soy base — wheat several times over. It splashes: shops often hand out a paper bib, and you should take it.

items.en: Curry udon with a breadcrumbed fried pork cutlet laid on top
items.note: The panko crust drinks up the curry gravy and collapses into it. Wheat in the noodle, the roux and the panko.

items.en: Udon with chicken and sweet grilled Japanese leek
items.note: 'Nanban' means the leek, not chilli — the negi is seared so it goes sweet and slightly smoky in the broth. 親子南ばん, the same with egg bound through it, is ¥800. Wheat noodle, wheat-soy broth.

items.en: Flat Nagoya kishimen with prawn tempura in the broth
items.note: The same tempura is available on udon or soba at ¥950; the ¥1,320 上 version gets a larger prawn. Wheat batter over a wheat noodle in a wheat-soy broth.

items.en: Udon simmered and served in its earthenware pot in a soy-based broth
items.note: Nikomi udon is cooked in the donabe rather than boiled separately, so the noodle stays stiff and chewy and thickens its own broth with released starch. Arrives at a violent boil and stays hot for ten minutes. Wheat noodle, wheat-soy broth.

items.en: Miso-nikomi udon — stiff unsalted wheat udon simmered in a dark hatchō-miso broth in an earthenware pot
items.note: The Nagoya dish. The noodles are made without salt so they can take the long simmer, which is why they stay so firm and slightly floury at the core — that texture is intended, not undercooking. Hatchō miso itself is only soybeans and salt, but the broth adds dashi and often soy sauce, and the noodle is wheat. Frequently served with a raw egg cracked in; the pot lid doubles as your bowl.

items.en: Old-school soy-broth ramen — the 'Chinese noodle' of a neighbourhood noodle shop
items.note: Not soba at all despite the name: alkaline wheat ramen noodles in a light soy broth with chashu, menma and leek. Miso ramen is ¥750 and the loaded chashu-men ¥820. Wheat noodle and wheat-soy broth.

items.en: Cold soba drained on a tray, eaten by dipping into a cup of chilled broth
items.note: The summer order. Wheat-blended buckwheat noodle and a wheat-soy dipping broth. A set version with a small rice dish is ¥1,080.

items.en: Cold kishimen on a tray with dipping broth — the flat Nagoya noodle served zaru-style
items.note: Chilling firms the wide ribbons and makes their slipperiness the whole experience — arguably the best way to meet kishimen. Wheat noodle, wheat-soy dipping broth.

items.en: Kishimen lifted straight from the boiling pot into its own hot cooking water, with a separate dipping broth
items.note: The style the shop names itself after — 手打釜揚うどん きよひら. Never rinsed, so the noodle keeps its surface starch and tastes strongly of wheat; you dip it into concentrated tsuyu. Kama-age zaru udon is the same price. Wheat noodle, wheat-soy tsuyu.

items.en: Cold kishimen on a tray with a plate of hot tempura
items.note: The top of the noodle list along with tempura kama-age kishimen at the same ¥1,540; plain ten-zaru soba is ¥1,510. Wheat batter, wheat noodle, wheat-soy tsuyu.

items.en: Chilled thin wheat noodles with dipping broth — summer only
items.note: Marked 夏期のみ on the card, so it is off the menu outside summer. Hiyamugi sits between somen and udon in thickness and is served on ice. Chilled udon is ¥870, chilled tempura udon ¥1,010. Wheat.

items.en: Nagoya miso-katsu over rice: a panko-crumbed pork cutlet under sweet dark hatchō-miso sauce
items.note: The Nagoya dish, in bowl form. The tare is built on hatchō miso — soybeans and salt only, no barley or rice koji — but it is let down with soy sauce, mirin, dashi and sugar, so the sauce is not wheat-free even though the miso is. The panko crust is wheat regardless.

items.en: Pork cutlet simmered with onion and egg in sweet soy dashi, served over rice
items.note: The Kanto-style katsudon rather than the miso one: the crust is deliberately allowed to go soft in the broth. Panko is wheat, and the simmering liquid is wheat soy. Oyakodon (chicken and egg) is also ¥870, tamago-don ¥720.

items.en: Tempura over rice, glazed with sweet soy tare — standard size
items.note: The 上 (larger) version is ¥1,550. Wheat batter and wheat-soy tare.

items.en: Curry udon as a set meal with rice and sides
items.note: The card marks the three noodle set meals 煮込み・ライス組 — nikomi-pot noodles plus rice. Kishimen and soba sets are ¥1,010 each; miso-katsu teishoku is ¥1,160 and the plain lunch teishoku ¥910. Rice on the side is the standard Nagoya way to eat a nikomi. Wheat throughout.

nagoya_wa_no_food_hall_hosa_ho_.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from the hall's own site (hosa.nagoya), read from the site's published CMS data so that each price stays attached to its own dish. Prices are tax-included for eat-in. Address confirmed: 名古屋市中区三の丸1-1-1, ground floor of the Nagoya Noh Theatre across from Nagoya Castle; open 10:00–17:00, L.O. 16:30.

items.en: Nagoya's flat, wide, ribbon-thin wheat noodle in a clear dashi broth
items.note: The hall's anchor dish and the right thing to order if you only eat one Nagoya noodle. Rolled thin and cut broad so it cooks in moments and carries more broth per mouthful than round udon — softer and more slippery, with less chew. Wheat noodle; the broth is bonito dashi and wheat soy.

items.en: Chilled kishimen scented with sudachi, a small sharp green citrus — summer only
items.note: Marked 夏季限定. Thin discs of sudachi float on the surface and the whole bowl smells of lime-and-yuzu. Wheat noodle, dashi broth.

items.en: Cold kishimen drained on a bamboo tray, eaten by dipping into concentrated tsuyu
items.note: Chilling firms the wide ribbons and makes their slipperiness the point of the dish. Wheat noodle, wheat-soy dipping broth.

items.ja: 名古屋天ざるきしめん
items.en: Cold kishimen on a tray with a plate of hot tempura alongside
items.note: Cold noodles and hot crisp tempura sharing one dipping broth. Wheat batter over a wheat noodle — the most wheat-dense order on the food side.

items.ja: 四季の旬野菜と海老天丼
items.romaji: shiki no shun-yasai to ebi tendon
items.en: Tempura rice bowl: two prawns and five seasonal vegetables over rice
items.section: 御膳・丼 (set meals & rice bowls)
items.note: The site specifies the count — 海老2本、季節の野菜5種 — so the vegetables rotate with the season and are the real interest. Wheat batter and a wheat-soy tare.

items.ja: 八丁味噌仕立て どて煮丼
items.en: Doteni over rice: beef tendon and offal stewed for hours in dark hatchō miso
items.section: 御膳・丼 (set meals & rice bowls)
items.note: A Nagoya izakaya staple in bowl form — sticky, sweet-savoury, almost jammy, usually finished with leek. Hatchō miso is soybeans and salt only, with no barley or rice koji, so the miso itself is clean; the stew adds soy sauce and mirin, which is what makes the dish wheat-bearing.

items.ja: 一色産 香ばし鰻丼（並）
items.en: Grilled eel from Isshiki over rice — standard size, half an eel
items.section: 御膳・丼 (set meals & rice bowls)
items.note: Isshiki in Nishio, an hour south of Nagoya, is one of Japan's biggest eel-farming towns and the local benchmark. The 上 (premium) size is two-thirds of an eel at ¥2,800. The eel is basted repeatedly with a wheat-soy tare as it grills, so it is not wheat-free.

items.ja: 一色産 ひつまぶし
items.en: Nagoya's signature eel dish: grilled eel chopped over rice in a wooden tub, eaten three ways
items.section: 御膳・丼 (set meals & rice bowls)
items.note: The ritual is the delight, so do it properly. Cross-cut the rice into quarters. Eat the first quarter plain, to taste the eel and the tare. Eat the second with the yakumi — spring onion, wasabi, nori — stirred through. Pour the dashi over the third and eat it as ochazuke, which is when the fat and the smoke really open up. Then eat the fourth whichever way you liked best. The tare is wheat soy, so not gluten-free.

items.ja: 黒毛和牛 ひつまぶし
items.en: The same three-stage tub, made with black wagyu beef instead of eel
items.section: 御膳・丼 (set meals & rice bowls)
items.note: A modern variation that works better than it sounds: the dashi poured over at the third stage renders the beef fat and turns the bowl into a clear, meaty soup. Same wheat-soy tare.

items.en: Half-and-half set: a small kishimen plus a small eel rice bowl
items.section: ハーフ&ハーフ (half and half)
items.note: The best-value way to try both Nagoya headline dishes in one sitting if you are only in the city a day. Wheat noodle plus wheat-soy eel tare.

items.en: Half-and-half set: a small kishimen plus a small tempura rice bowl
items.section: ハーフ&ハーフ (half and half)
items.note: Wheat noodle and wheat batter.

items.en: Half-and-half set: a small kishimen plus a small hatchō-miso doteni bowl
items.section: ハーフ&ハーフ (half and half)
items.note: The cheapest of the three half-sets and the most local pairing of the lot. Wheat noodle; the doteni carries soy sauce as well as miso.

items.ja: 四季めぐる天ぷら盛り
items.en: A side plate of tempura — prawn and seasonal vegetables
items.note: The only à-la-carte savoury item, meant to be added to a noodle. Wheat batter, shared fryer.

items.en: Children's set meal, the larger of two
items.note: Set B is ¥1,000. Contents are not published; the hall asks about allergies at the counter.

items.ja: 濃厚抹茶ともちもち白玉
items.en: Chewy rice-flour dumplings with a thick matcha syrup, served with hōjicha
items.note: Shiratama are made from glutinous rice flour, so the dumplings themselves are rice, not wheat — but this is a kitchen that fries tempura and boils wheat kishimen all day, so ask before treating it as safe. The house matcha syrup is described as free of the bitterness and astringency you get from cheap matcha; pour on as much as you like.

items.ja: 黒蜜きな粉ともちもち白玉
items.en: Chewy rice-flour dumplings dusted in roasted soybean flour, with black sugar syrup
items.note: The kuromitsu is blended from Okinawan black sugar and kibi cane sugar. Rice flour and soybean flour only — the most plant-based sweet on the list — but it comes with hōjicha and shares a wheat-heavy kitchen, so confirm.

items.ja: だし香る甘醤油のもちもち白玉
items.romaji: dashi kaoru amajōyu no mochimochi shiratama
items.en: Chewy rice-flour dumplings in a dashi-scented sweet soy glaze (mitarashi)
items.note: Made with the hall's own ichiban-dashi, so it is savoury-sweet rather than simply sugary; the counter suggests dusting it with sanshō pepper or shichimi, which is worth doing. The dumplings are rice flour but the glaze is wheat soy and bonito dashi.

items.en: Two of the three shiratama flavours on one plate — pick any two
items.note: Choose from matcha, kuromitsu-kinako and the dashi sweet-soy. Hōjicha included. If the sweet-soy is one of your two, the plate carries wheat soy and dashi.

items.ja: 濃厚抹茶のマスカルポーネクリーム
items.en: Shaved ice with dense matcha syrup, mascarpone cream and a yuzu jelly base
items.note: Full size ¥1,300, half ¥1,000, hōjicha included. The yuzu jelly hidden under the ice is what keeps it from cloying — you find it near the end. The other standing flavour is a three-blend Japanese black tea with spices, also ¥1,300 / ¥1,000; two more rotate in and out (strawberry with matcha pudding, and roast-sweet-potato cream with black sesame blancmange). Dairy, so not vegan; ask about the kitchen if wheat matters.

items.ja: 和菓子とお抹茶セット（大黒屋本店）
items.en: A seasonal Japanese sweet with a bowl of whisked matcha
items.note: hosa is a hall with several separate businesses under one roof; this comes from Daikokuya Honten, a Nishiki 3-chōme confectioner of about 150 years that specialises in rakugan pressed-sugar sweets. Wagashi are typically rice flour, bean paste and sugar but wheat flour is common in the doughs and glutinous coatings, so do not assume gluten-free; egg and dairy also appear.

items.ja: 季節の生菓子（大黒屋本店）
items.en: A fresh seasonal wagashi, shaped and coloured to the month
items.note: Namagashi are the ones made to be eaten the same day and sculpted to a seasonal motif — a maple leaf, a plum blossom. Warabimochi from the same counter is also ¥600. Bean paste and rice or wheat flour depending on the sweet; ask which.

items.ja: ふわふわわぬき あんバター（なか又）
items.en: A very soft dorayaki pancake sandwich filled with bean paste and butter
items.note: From Nakamata, a Gunma confectioner whose 'fuwafuwa wanuki' dorayaki draws queues around the country; hosa is its first permanent counter outside Gunma. Dorayaki pancakes are wheat flour and egg, so this is squarely wheat.

items.ja: あんトースト最中（お土産・花桔梗）
items.en: Take-home monaka wafers with a bean-paste-and-butter 'ogura toast' filling
items.note: From Hanakikyō, which traces its line to Kikyōya, confectioner to the Owari Tokugawa lords, so this is about as Nagoya as a souvenir gets — a monaka riff on ogura toast, the city's thick buttered toast with sweet azuki. Monaka wafers are pressed from glutinous rice, but the filling and the toast reference both point at wheat and dairy; sold boxed to take away.

items.ja: お抹茶 和三盆糖付
items.en: A bowl of whisked matcha served with a wasanbon sugar sweet, iced or hot
items.note: Wasanbon is a fine-grained Shikoku sugar pressed into small dry shapes that dissolve on the tongue — eat it first, then drink. Matcha latte ¥650 (¥800 iced), Japanese black tea ¥600, the house 蓬左 blend coffee ¥600, decaf ¥600, café latte ¥650. On the alcohol list: Asahi Super Dry bottle ¥750, Kamoshibito Kuheiji junmai daiginjō from Nagoya ¥1,200, Chita whisky ¥1,000 — note the shōchū 一粒の麦 is barley-based.

nagoya_kabuto.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from the restaurant's own current site (kabuto-aichi.com/food), which notes the listed prices took effect from December; all prices tax-included. The sample course below is the shop's own published お品書き for the ¥14,000 course and rotates with the season. Address confirmed: 名古屋市西区那古野1-30-6, Shikemichi.

items.note: Kabuto has served nothing but chef's-choice courses, by reservation only, for twenty-five years — there is no à la carte, so the course is the menu. The owner-chef trained in French kitchens for over twenty years before opening a Japanese one, and the cooking is a kaiseki skeleton with French technique in the joints. Tell them about allergies when you book, not on arrival.

items.en: Chef's-choice dinner course, middle grade — the one the published sample menu belongs to
items.note: Around eleven courses from appetiser to coffee. This is the tier whose sample お品書き the restaurant publishes, so it is the one you can actually picture before you go.
Same shape, more expensive materials — the chef buys at market himself each morning and brings in luxury ingredients from around the country.
Lunch is a single 11:30–13:00 seating, so you are expected to arrive at the start. The cheapest way into a restaurant that is otherwise an evening proposition.
Named for the chef, Kabuto Sumio. Effectively the dinner 梅 course at lunchtime.

items.en: Special lunch menu, arranged on request
items.note: Priced from ¥13,000 upward; used for formal occasions — the restaurant is often booked for engagement meetings between two families, memorial meals and business entertaining, and has private rooms upstairs for six and a table for four.

items.ja: 秋季限定 松茸料理
items.note: Mid-October to late November only. Matsutake is Japan's most expensive mushroom and is prized for smell rather than taste — pine, cinnamon, something almost like petrol — which is why it is usually barely cooked: grilled over charcoal, steamed in a clay teapot, or in rice. The course uses the whole mushroom across several dishes.

items.ja: 前菜：牡蠣のきらず和え
items.en: Appetiser — oysters dressed with okara, the soft soy pulp left over from making tofu
items.section: お品書き 一例 (sample course, ¥14,000 tier)
items.note: 'Kirazu' is an old, more polite word for okara. It is dry and faintly nutty and it soaks up the oyster liquor, which stops the oyster tasting merely salty. Usually seasoned with vinegar and a little soy — ask.

items.en: Appetiser — savoury steamed egg custard with pufferfish
items.section: お品書き 一例 (sample course, ¥14,000 tier)
items.note: Chawanmushi is egg loosened with dashi until it barely sets — eaten with a spoon, somewhere between soup and custard. Fugu is lean and springy and holds its texture in the steam. Dashi and usually a little light soy.

items.ja: 向付：おこぜの重ね盛り
items.en: Sashimi course — stonefish sliced and layered
items.section: お品書き 一例 (sample course, ¥14,000 tier)
items.note: Okoze is an ugly, spiny reef fish with unusually firm, sweet white flesh; it is sliced very thin because of the texture. Mukōzuke is the sashimi course, placed on the far side of the tray. The dipping soy is wheat soy unless you ask.

items.en: Soup course — shiitake steamed with dashi in a small clay teapot
items.section: お品書き 一例 (sample course, ¥14,000 tier)
items.note: Dobin-mushi arrives as a lidded teapot with a small cup and a wedge of citrus. Pour the broth into the cup, squeeze the citrus in and drink it first; then lift the lid and eat the solids with chopsticks. The aroma released when you open it is the whole design.

items.en: Grilled course — langoustine grilled under a sea-urchin glaze
items.section: お品書き 一例 (sample course, ¥14,000 tier)
items.note: Akaza-ebi is the Japanese langoustine — sweeter and more delicate than prawn. Uni-yaki means the sea urchin is whipped, usually with egg yolk, and painted on before the grill so it sets into a rich orange crust. A very French move in a Japanese course.

items.ja: 炊合せ：鮑、生麩、筍、菜の花、さといもの炊合せ
items.romaji: takiawase: awabi, namafu, takenoko, nanohana, satoimo
items.en: Simmered course — abalone, fresh wheat gluten cake, bamboo shoot, rape blossom and taro, each cooked separately then plated together
items.section: お品書き 一例 (sample course, ¥14,000 tier)
items.note: Takiawase means each element is simmered in its own broth to its own doneness and only meets on the plate — the technique that separates kaiseki from stew. Note the namafu: fresh fu is made from wheat gluten, so this course is definitively not wheat-free even before the soy.

items.ja: 肉料理：厳選和牛のヒレ肉ステーキのたたき、花山葵添え
items.romaji: nikuryōri: wagyū hire steak no tataki, hanawasabi-zoe
items.en: Meat course — wagyu fillet seared hard outside and left raw within, with flowering wasabi
items.section: お品書き 一例 (sample course, ¥14,000 tier)
items.note: Tataki means seared only at the surface then sliced, so you get a crust and a raw centre in the same mouthful. Hanawasabi is the flowering stem of the wasabi plant, briefly blanched — hot in a green, mustardy way quite unlike the paste. Ask about the sauce; ponzu and soy are the usual partners.

items.en: Rice course — sea bream over rice with hot tea or dashi poured over
items.section: お品書き 一例 (sample course, ¥14,000 tier)
items.note: The rice course that closes a kaiseki. The bream is usually first dressed in a sesame-and-soy sauce, then the hot liquid is poured over so it half-cooks at the table — the moment the aroma lifts is the point. Wheat soy in the dressing.

items.section: お品書き 一例 (sample course, ¥14,000 tier)
items.note: A clear dashi soup with one or two ingredients in it, served alongside the rice course; the sample menu names an ingredient (printed as ギニス) that is not a standard term, so ask at the table what is in it that day. Bonito dashi and light soy.

items.en: Fruit course — cherimoya, the custard apple
items.section: お品書き 一例 (sample course, ¥14,000 tier)
items.note: A green scaled tropical fruit whose white flesh tastes like banana, pineapple and vanilla custard at once, eaten with a spoon. Plain fresh fruit — nothing added, so this one course is genuinely free of both wheat and animal products. An unusual thing to meet in a Japanese course and very much this chef's French streak.

items.ja: コーヒー（古代チーズ『蘇』と共に）
items.en: Coffee served with 'so' — an ancient Japanese cheese first made in the Asuka period
items.section: お品書き 一例 (sample course, ¥14,000 tier)
items.note: So is milk boiled down for hours until it thickens into a fudgy, faintly caramelised solid — the oldest recorded dairy product in Japan, from the 7th century, and a genuinely strange and lovely way to close the meal. Dairy, so not vegan. If you ask, the chef will whisk matcha for you afterwards in the tea room, for a small extra charge.
Barley malt, so not gluten-free. Premium Malt's and Kirin Ichiban Shibori are ¥800 each.

items.ja: ノンアルコールビール
items.note: Still brewed from barley malt — alcohol-free is not gluten-free.
Leaf tea and hot water only. The drinks list also covers sake, shōchū (barley and sweet potato), bottled and glass wine, plum wine and soft drinks; corkage on your own bottle is ¥3,000.

nagoya_sushi_shimizu.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Course price from the restaurant's own site and its shop-managed Tabelog page (¥22,000 tax-included, raised from ¥20,000 pre-tax on 1 April 2025). Drink prices transcribed from a photograph of the shop's own drink card, 2025/07 — those are quoted before tax. Address confirmed: 名古屋市西区名西2-10-10-1.

items.en: The only menu: a chef's-choice course of roughly twenty plates, reservation-only
items.note: There is nothing else to order. The shape is fixed: about nine tsumami (small cooked and dressed dishes, changed monthly) first, then eleven or twelve pieces of nigiri. Chef Shimizu Naoki keeps the rice balls small so the course does not overwhelm, which is why sixteen to seventeen plates still eats lightly. Tell them any allergy or dislike when you book. Cancel less than seven days out and you may be charged in full. No strong perfume — they ask on the website. Wheat soy is used throughout a sushi counter, in the nikiri brush-on sauce as much as the dipping dish.

items.en: Lunch omakase — a shorter, sushi-led version of the course
items.note: Not a regular service: the shop opens for lunch only two or three times a year, on an irregular schedule, and it is announced rather than scheduled. Price from a first-hand November 2025 report. Standard hours are evenings only, 18:30–23:00 on weekdays and 18:00 at weekends.

items.en: Tuna bought from Yamayuki, the Toyosu market's most famous tuna wholesaler
items.note: Yamayuki is the intermediate wholesaler that repeatedly wins the New Year first-tuna auction, and the shop names it explicitly on its own site. On the counter the fish sits on a card giving its port and its catch method — a recent one read Fukushima, Nakanosaku, longline. The chū-toro is the piece to watch for. Brushed with nikiri (thinned wheat soy) rather than dipped.

items.en: Squid, scored and pressed onto the rice
items.note: The shop describes it as beautifully translucent, with a clinging, melting texture and a deep sweetness. Good squid is scored with a fine grid so it releases that sweetness and is not rubbery. Often finished with salt and sudachi rather than soy — worth asking.

items.en: White tilefish cured between sheets of kombu
items.note: Kobujime draws water out of the fish and pushes kombu glutamate in — the flesh firms, the flavour concentrates and it picks up a faint marine perfume. Shiro-amadai is the most prized of the tilefish and is rarely served raw. Kombu and salt only in the cure itself.

items.en: Sea urchin, served with salt instead of soy
items.note: The shop says it chooses the urchin partly on colour and serves it with salt specifically so nothing masks the urchin's own taste — a deliberate choice, since soy is the default. That also makes it one of the few pieces not carrying wheat soy, though the rice and the counter are shared.

items.en: Gizzard shad, cured in salt then vinegar
items.note: The Edomae benchmark: a small silver fish that must be cured exactly right, and the piece by which sushi chefs are judged. The shop describes its work as finding the precise balance of salt and vinegar so the fish's own savour survives. Rice vinegar, not wheat — but the nikiri brushed on is wheat soy.

items.en: Hand roll of house-cured mullet roe with a piece of seasonal grilled fish, passed to you directly
items.note: The shop's own specialité, and Tabelog's editors single it out too. Karasumi is salted, pressed, air-dried grey mullet roe — dense, waxy, intensely savoury, like a marine bottarga. Paired with a grilled fish of the day, one report naming grilled nodoguro, whose melting fat plays against the roe's salt. Handed over the counter to be eaten immediately, nori still crisp.

items.en: Simmered clam from Kuwana, laid over the rice as the last nigiri
items.note: Kuwana in Mie, an hour west, has been famous for its hamaguri clams since the Edo period. The clam is poached gently and glazed with its own reduced cooking liquor — a classic Edomae finish, and here a plump, broad piece that ends the nigiri run. The glaze (tsume) is built on soy and mirin, so it is wheat.

items.en: The closing roll: dried gourd shavings simmered sweet, rolled in nori and rice
items.note: The shop calls this its fixed finish and says the pleasure is deliberately quiet — the boil is timed so the gourd keeps some bite, and the seasoning is judged to soak just far enough. Kanpyō is shaved dried calabash; it is simmered in soy, sugar and mirin, so it is wheat-bearing but contains no animal product beyond that.

items.ja: 生ビール 白穂乃香（サッポロ）
items.en: Draught Shiro Honoka — Sapporo's unfiltered cloudy wheat-ish lager
items.note: A rare unpasteurised draught only available on tap at selected accounts. Barley malt, so not gluten-free. Small draught ¥600. Prices on this card are before tax.
Asahi in the same size is also ¥900. Barley malt.

items.ja: ノンアルコール（アサヒゼロ）
items.note: Alcohol-free but still brewed from barley malt.

items.en: Kamoshibito Kuheiji, the local Nagoya sake, by the 180ml cup
items.note: Brewed in Nagoya itself and one of the few Japanese sakes with a real following in France, where the same house also makes wine. Rice, water, koji and yeast — no wheat, no animal product. Priced from ¥1,600 per 1-gō depending on the bottle open that night.

items.en: Kokuryū from Fukui, by the 180ml cup
items.note: A Fukui house with a long reputation for elegant, restrained daiginjō — a natural partner for a light, vinegar-forward sushi course. The card also offers a 本日の銘酒 (bottle of the day) from ¥1,600 and 720ml bottles from ¥5,000.

items.ja: 誠鏡 純米たけはら（広島）
items.section: お飲み物 熱燗 (warmed sake)
items.note: One of two sakes the shop lists specifically for warming; the other is Bōjimaya chōkarakuchi from Gifu at ¥1,300. Warming a junmai broadens it and makes it sit better with the richer, cooked tsumami early in the course.

items.section: お飲み物 ウイスキー (whisky)
items.note: Distilled from malted barley. Chita ¥1,200, Ichiro's Malt ¥900, mizunara-finished ¥900, Dewar's ¥800. Add ¥100 to have any spirit topped with soda.

items.section: お飲み物 ソフトドリンク (soft drinks)
items.note: Worth knowing before you sit down: a notice on the card dated 1 June 2025 says guests who do not order a drink are charged for the green tea as a cover. Perrier ¥750, black oolong ¥700, cola and dry ginger ale ¥600.

nagoya_the_bar_castle.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from the bar's own August menu PDF published on the hotel site, read positionally so each price stays with its own item, plus the hotel's own TableCheck booking page. All prices include 10% consumption tax; a further 15% service charge is added. Address confirmed: 4F, ESPACIO Nagoya Castle, 3-19 Hinokuchi-chō, Nishi-ku.

items.ja: 名古屋チーズ盛り合わせ
items.en: Assorted local cheeses: mozzarella with wasabi stems, aonori-seaweed grilled cheese, gouda and ricotta, with a milk-caramel sauce made from whey
items.note: The one plate that argues for this being a Nagoya bar rather than a generic hotel one — wasabi stems and aonori seaweed worked into Italian-style cheeses, and the caramel made from the whey the cheesemaking leaves behind. Cheese itself is wheat-free; ask what it is served with, since crackers and bread are the usual bed.

items.ja: プロシュート・ディ・パルマと飛騨清見キルノンチュエ シャルキュトリー・サレゾン
items.romaji: prosciutto di Parma to Hida Kiyomi Kirnonchue charcuterie salaison
items.en: Charcuterie board: Parma ham alongside cured meats from Kirnonchue in Hida Kiyomi
items.note: Kirnonchue is a well-regarded charcutier in the mountains of northern Gifu, so this pairs an Italian benchmark against a Japanese one. Dry-cured meat is normally wheat-free but starters and casings vary — ask, and ask what bread comes with it.

items.ja: 名古屋コーチン砂肝のスパイシーコンフィ
items.romaji: Nagoya Cochin sunagimo no spicy confit
items.en: Nagoya Cochin chicken gizzards confited slowly in fat with spices
items.note: Nagoya Cochin is the city's heritage chicken breed — darker, firmer and far more flavoured than commodity chicken, and a genuine local speciality. Gizzard is all muscle, so the long low confit is what makes it tender rather than rubbery. Confit is usually just fat, salt and spice; ask about the spice blend.

items.ja: 「渥美プレミアムラスサーモン」のマリネ ラス・エル・ハヌートの香り
items.romaji: Atsumi premium russ salmon no marine, ras el hanout no kaori
items.en: Marinated salmon farmed on the Atsumi peninsula, scented with ras el hanout
items.note: Local fish from Tahara in Aichi, dressed with the North African spice blend ras el hanout — which fits the room, since the bar is lit by Moroccan lamps. Marinades at this level are usually citrus, oil and spice, but ask whether soy is in it.

items.ja: ロメインレタスと愛知みかわ豚ベーコンのシーザーサラダ
items.romaji: romaine lettuce to Aichi Mikawa-buta bacon no Caesar salad
items.en: Caesar salad with romaine and bacon from Aichi Mikawa pork
items.note: Caesar dressing carries anchovy and egg and the salad normally arrives with croutons, so it is neither wheat-free nor vegetarian as standard.

items.ja: 5種の野菜スティック もろみ味噌ディップ
items.romaji: 5-shu no yasai stick, moromi miso dip
items.en: Five raw vegetables cut into batons with a moromi-miso dip
items.note: Moromi miso is the coarse, still-chunky mash from part-way through fermentation — sweeter and looser than finished miso, eaten as a dip rather than cooked. It is normally built on barley or wheat koji, which is exactly why it is not gluten-free; the vegetables themselves are.

items.ja: 愛知県産カラフルトマトとチェリーモッツァレラチーズのカプレーゼ 豊橋産大葉のジェノベーゼ
items.romaji: Aichi-san colourful tomato to cherry mozzarella no caprese, Toyohashi-san ōba no genovese
items.en: Caprese of Aichi tomatoes and cherry mozzarella with a pesto made from shiso instead of basil
items.note: The shiso pesto is the clever part — ōba has the same green herbal lift as basil but with an aniseed edge, and it is grown intensively around Toyohashi. Dairy, so not vegan; genovese usually contains cheese and nuts too.

items.ja: 愛知みかわ豚ロースハムと名古屋コーチン卵のホットミックスサンド
items.romaji: Aichi Mikawa-buta loin ham to Nagoya Cochin tamago no hot mix sandwich
items.en: Hot sandwich of Mikawa pork loin ham and Nagoya Cochin egg
items.note: The bar's substantial order if you want something that eats like a meal. Bread, so wheat.

items.ja: トリュフ香るフレンチフライポテト オニオンディップとオーガニックケチャップ
items.en: Truffle-scented fries with onion dip and organic ketchup
items.note: Potato and oil, so the fries themselves need not contain wheat — but a hotel bar fryer is shared with breaded items, and the onion dip is dairy. Ask if it matters.

items.ja: 中東風ひよこ豆のコロッケ「ファラフェル」タヒニ風味噌ソース
items.romaji: chūtō-fū hiyokomame no croquette 'falafel', tahini-fū miso sauce
items.en: Falafel — Middle Eastern chickpea fritters — with a tahini-and-miso sauce
items.note: Falafel is ground chickpea, herbs and spice, so it is normally free of both wheat and animal products — but the miso in the sauce may be barley-based, the fryer is shared, and hotel versions often bind with flour. The nearest thing on the card to a plant-based order. Worth knowing before you ask: the hotel will build a low-allergen version of some dishes excluding the 9 declared allergens (wheat among them) if you request it when booking, but it states in writing that everything is cooked in one kitchen with shared equipment, that trace contamination is possible, and that its food is therefore not fully allergy-safe — it may decline to serve you if your reaction is severe.
The cheapest thing to put on the table with a drink. Nuts and smoke, in principle — ask about the seasoning, since soy and butter coatings are both common.

items.ja: 愛知県南知多町の海老せんべい
items.en: Prawn crackers from Minamichita in Aichi
items.note: Minamichita on the Chita peninsula is Japan's centre for ebi-senbei, pressed from whole prawn and starch. Cheap-tasting elsewhere, very good when it is the real thing. Prawn crackers are normally potato or tapioca starch but wheat starch is common in the binder, and there is prawn in them.

items.ja: オリーブと地場産野菜のピクルス
items.romaji: olive to jibasan yasai no pickles
items.note: Vinegar-pickled vegetables and olives — usually plant-based and wheat-free, but pickling liquors often carry soy or dashi in a Japanese kitchen; ask.

items.ja: 名古屋コーチン卵のプリン
items.en: Custard pudding made with Nagoya Cochin eggs
items.section: フードメニュー デザート (dessert)
items.note: Cochin eggs have deep orange yolks and make an unusually rich, yellow purin. Egg, milk and caramel — no wheat in a classic purin, but confirm nothing is served on the side.

items.ja: チョコレートテリーヌ
items.section: フードメニュー デザート (dessert)
items.note: Terrines are usually chocolate, butter and egg with little or no flour, but recipes vary — ask. Dried fruit ¥2,200, a chocolate tablet selection ¥2,600 and a fresh fruit plate ¥4,000 sit alongside.

items.ja: ショートカクテル 各種
items.en: Short cocktails, all one price — gimlet, martini, cosmopolitan, espresso martini, yukiguni, daiquiri, casablanca, margarita, manhattan, sidecar, jack rose, after dinner
items.section: カクテル ショート (short cocktails)
items.note: The card prints the base spirits for each — useful if you are avoiding something. Yukiguni ('snow country') is the one to know: a 1958 Japanese competition winner of vodka, Cointreau and lime with a sugar-frosted rim, and a fixture of every serious Japanese bar. Distilled spirits are generally considered wheat-free even when grain-based, but whisk(e)y- and beer-derived ingredients are not — ask if you are strict.

items.en: Gin and tonic with fresh lime
items.section: カクテル ロング (long cocktails)
items.note: The long list also runs negroni ¥2,100, moscow mule ¥2,100, el diablo ¥2,100, old fashioned ¥2,100 and spumoni ¥2,100.

items.en: Rum, mint, fresh lime, soda and sugar syrup
items.section: カクテル ロング (long cocktails)
items.note: Salty dog is the same ¥2,200. The terrace, where you drink this looking at the floodlit castle keep, is the reason to come at this hour rather than any other.

items.ja: フレンチ75 / シャンパンカクテル
items.section: カクテル ロング (long cocktails)
items.note: French 75 is gin, champagne, lemon and sugar; the champagne cocktail is a sugar cube soaked in bitters with champagne poured over. Both ¥2,900.

items.ja: ノンアルコールカクテル 各種
items.en: Alcohol-free cocktails: non-alcoholic gin and tonic, cool collins, cinderella, virgin breeze
items.note: All ¥1,900, all fruit-and-soda based. Non-alcoholic beer (Bière des Amis Blonde) is ¥2,200 and is barley-based, unlike these.

items.section: ジャパニーズウイスキー (Japanese whisky)
items.note: Malted barley. The Japanese list is deep and priced by 45ml pour: Yamazaki and Hakushu ¥2,800, their 12-year ¥4,200, their 18-year ¥12,100; Hibiki Japanese Harmony ¥2,800, Hibiki 21 ¥13,000, Chita ¥2,600. There is also a standing bottle offer — Yamazaki 12 at ¥42,000 the bottle, Macallan 12 at ¥39,000, limited numbers.

items.ja: 夏のカクテルプレート（ピエール・エルメ・パリ スイーツと）
items.romaji: natsu no cocktail plate (Pierre Hermé Paris sweets to)
items.en: Seasonal cocktail-and-pâtisserie plate: one summer cocktail with three Pierre Hermé sweets
items.note: Served 17:00 onward. Choose either a watermelon-and-vodka 'Midsummer Salty' or a frozen daiquiri of rum, shine-muscat grape, melon liqueur and pear syrup; it comes with a Macaron Infiniment Citron stamped with the hotel's logo, an Ispahan bonbon chocolat and an amande noire. Macarons are almond-based but Pierre Hermé does not make them in a gluten-free facility, and the plate contains egg and dairy.

items.ja: ミッドサマー・アフタヌーンティー
items.en: Afternoon tea with savouries, scones and eight fruit pâtisseries, free-flow drinks
items.section: アフタヌーンティー (afternoon tea, 12:00–17:00)
items.note: The bar is a different place before 17:00. Two sittings, 12:00 and 14:30, produced with Atelier UKAI: chilled corn soup, summer ratatouille and an edamame corte on the savoury side, then pineapple-mint tart, melon shortcake, muscat-and-plum jelly, peach verrine, mango éclair and a coconut-passionfruit mousse. Free-flow Ronnefeldt teas, mocktails and coffee. The scones are the giveaway on wheat — one wholemeal, one flavoured with hatchō miso, which is a genuinely Nagoyan touch. Declare any allergy when you book rather than on arrival — the hotel says it cannot always accommodate a request made after you sit down. A yukata-dressing plan built around the same tea runs ¥18,500. After 17:00 the room is 20-and-over only.

nagoya_chambre_d_enfants.price_note: Drinks transcribed from the shop's own printed card photographed 2026/07 (an identical copy was shot 2026/05); a 10% service charge is added on top. The food is a single daily omakase whose price the shop does not publish anywhere reachable — Tabelog's dinner band is ¥20,000–¥29,999 and a 2026 diner reports ¥32,910 all-in with drinks, so the course price is left blank rather than guessed. The dish list below is the printed card for one seating, 19 août 2026, and rotates every service. Prices approximate — may change.

items.ja: おまかせコース（日替わり）
items.en: Chef's tasting menu — the only food option, rewritten every service
items.note: 価格は非公開。食べログのディナー予算帯は¥20,000〜¥29,999、飲み物込み¥32,910の報告あり。フレンチなのでバター・生クリーム・フォンを使う。Tabelog French Hyakumeiten EAST 2025; hard to book. Raise gluten when you reserve, not on the night — the menu is written per service so they can work round it.
日本在来のいちじく。フレンチではハムや生ハム、乳製品と合わせることが多い。The card names only the ingredient, which is this kitchen's style.
白身の高級魚。生かマリネで出ることが多い。Usually served raw or lightly cured.
イカ自体は小麦なし。ソースの繋ぎを要確認。
ビスクやアメリケーヌはブール・マニエ（小麦＋バター）でとろみをつけることがある。Classic French shellfish sauces are often thickened with a flour-and-butter beurre manié — this is the plate to ask about.
骨切りした鱧。湯引きなら小麦なし、粉をはたいて焼く／揚げるなら不可。A midsummer delicacy; safe poached, not if floured.
高級白身魚。ソースのとろみの付け方を要確認。
パイ生地は小麦粉とバター。The one certain gluten dish on this card — a 2026 diner describes eel baked in pastry. Ask for a substitute when you book.
鴨のソースはフォンと赤ワインが基本で小麦なしのことが多いが要確認。
果物のデザート。クッキー・スポンジ・チュイルが添えられることがある。
晩夏の桃。同上。
小菓子はほぼ確実に小麦・バター・卵。Petits fours are essentially always wheat, butter and egg.

nagoya_shogetsu_shikemichi.price_note: Course prices are from the shop's own site, whose page was last modified 2026-06-23; tax included (※全て税込価格). A ¥1,700 tempura-teishoku lunch photographed 2024/09 (and ¥1,500 in 2022) has gone from the site: treat it as discontinued rather than ordering it. Prices approximate — may change.
